objective: gorilla/mux returns an inconsistent HTTP status when a path is registered under multiple methods and a GET request fails only the GET route's query-value constraint. Per HTTP semantics the router should surface Not Found (ErrNotFound / 404) because no route fully matches the request, but mux instead leaves ErrMethodMismatch (405) set from the sibling POST route. Make Route.Match conform to the correct status: when a candidate route matches the path/method but its query constraint is unsatisfied, a lingering ErrMethodMismatch from other candidates must be cleared so the router reports ErrNotFound, while a genuine method-only mismatch on a valid path still reports ErrMethodMismatch.

explorationSubQuestions.question: In gorilla/mux Route.Match at this pinned revision, when a path/method candidate route is rejected because its query constraint is unsatisfied, is a match.MatchErr==ErrMethodMismatch (set by a sibling method-only route) cleared, and what is the correct HTTP status the router should ultimately report for that request?
explorationSubQuestions.groundTruth: At this revision the query-mismatch branch does NOT clear a sibling ErrMethodMismatch, so the router wrongly reports 405; the conforming fix clears match.MatchErr to nil in that branch when it is ErrMethodMismatch, so the outer matcher reports ErrNotFound (404) since no route fully matches.
